text:
maria: Heads up — seeing steady memory growth on rwd-rt-12 during a long streaming chat run that exercises tool loops. Host goes from ~12GB to ~28GB over ~90 minutes. Not typical spike, slow climb. :thinking:

kai: Can you share the run config and model? streaming=true, tool_loop=yes, batch_size=1?

maria: Model: rwd-instruct-13B-v2 (quantized). Config: continuous_streaming=true, kv_cache=on, autoshrink=enabled but set to conservative thresholds. Tool loop repeatedly calls external tool that returns structured payloads; each tool call appends tokens to the context, so long contexts (50k+ tokens).

josh: Any jemalloc/arena churn visible? Can you paste `mallctl` stats or `jeprof` snapshot?

maria: Pasted quick `pmap` + runtime log snippet:

```
> pmap rwd-rt-12 | tail -n 3
00007f7c0000-7f9c0000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0  [heap]
size: 12.1g -> 28.3g over 5400s
\n[rt] kv_cache.resident_entries=1_240_000
[rt] kv_cache.evictions=4_812
[rt] kv_cache.eviction_loop_delay=disabled
[rt] streaming.inflight_sessions=27
[rt] toolloop.calls_per_session=1123
```
\nkai: Hmm eviction count low vs resident_entries high. Eviction_loop seems disabled? Why is that off?

maria: autoshrink config set evict_threshold=0.9 and backpressure_pause true, so eviction coroutine shouldn't run while streams marked 'pinned'. I think pinned entries = entries referenced by in-flight streams (maybe not being released).

jen: Could be fragmentation (lots of small allocations from KV nodes) or a true leak (objects still reachable). Do a heap snapshot with `heaptrack` and also a `malloc_stats` dump when resident count high.

maria: Ran heaptrack, attached top hotspots (abbrev):

```
heaptrack top: allocs in runtime::KVNode::allocate
  42% by runtime::kv_store::insert_from_stream
  18% by streaming::tool_loop::append_tokens
  12% by json::serialize
```

josh: That points to allocations indeed coming from streaming path. Are we reusing KVNode objects or always allocating new ones per token range?

maria: Code uses `KVNode::from_slice` which currently allocates a new node when the appended slice crosses a shard boundary. Tool payloads are frequently 3-8 tokens and cross shards a lot. We intended to recycle via slab allocator but that code path is gated behind `reuse_fastpath` which doesn't trigger for fragmented slices.

kai: Two hypotheses: 1) reuse fastpath not matching due to copy/offset invariants introduced by quantized model's KV layout; 2) eviction not running because the entries are considered pinned by in-flight stream refs. Either would cause growth.

alloc-bot: Observed repeating allocation callstack signature: runtime::KVNode::allocate -> arena_alloc -> jemalloc.

maria: Reproducer: run `./perf/repro_stream --tool-loop --tokens 60k --parallel 30` on staging; memory climbs linearly and does not fall until sessions finish.

jen: Quick check: can you add a debug log printing `kv_node.refcount` when we finish serializing an outbound chunk? If refcounts never hit zero, there's a borrowing bug.

maria: Added logs, sample: `kv_node[0x7fffa12c].refcount=1` after chunk flushed. Should be 0.

josh: That is concrete. Where is the refcount incremented? Likely in the streaming iterator that pins ranges during async tool call. Maybe we forgot to `drop()` a guard in `on_tool_response`.

kai: Also confirm eviction coroutine condition: it checks `inflight_sessions==0 || force_eviction==true`. So eviction disabled while inflight>0. That was a design choice to avoid evicting needed prefixes, but with long contexts it means memory can grow unbounded. We should change to allow eviction of least-recently-used entries not referenced by active iterators even when inflight>0.

maria: Agreed. Proposed immediate mitigations:
- re-enable eviction for unreferenced entries even with inflight sessions (fast fix)
- ensure streaming iterator releases refs on chunk send (bug fix)
- add periodic sampling of `resident_entries` and trigger aggressive compaction when > 75% of limit

jen: Also add a debug mode that treats refcounts with ASAN/UBSAN to catch use-after-free if we change pinning semantics.

maria: I pushed a patch branch `fix/kv-release-on-chunk` that drops the guard in `on_tool_response` and added a unit test reproducer. Patch reduces leak in staging run: 12.1g -> 13.5g steady vs 28g before.

josh: Nice. Can we also add a small slab-based freelist for common node sizes so allocation churn reduces fragmentation? That will cut peak by ~10-15% in my microbench.

kai: Long term: update eviction policy to consult iterator weak-refs and GC unreachable nodes asynchronously. Short-term: re-enable selective eviction and add safety metrics/alerts (resident_entries_delta > X per minute).

maria: Rolling the patch to canary now. Will monitor resident_entries, p99 latency, and tool loop error rates.

jen: If canary looks good, schedule an A/B to Dedicated customers to validate no regressions. Also file a perf-regression ticket for kernel selection impact (alloc/free pattern may affect kernel choices).

maria: Thanks all. I'll paste canary logs in this thread. :thumbsup:
